nist63.title: Evaluation Inputs
nist63.statement: At a minimum, evaluation inputs SHALL include: (a) Integrated CSP, IdP, and authentication functions as well as validation, verification, and fraud management systems, as appropriate; (b) Customer feedback mechanisms, such as complaint processes, helpdesk statistics, and other user feedback (e.g., surveys, interviews, or focus groups); (c) Threat analysis, threat reporting, and threat intelligence feeds that are available; (d) Fraud trends, fraud investigation results, and fraud metrics as available; and (e) The results of ongoing customer experience assessments and privacy assessments.

nist63.title: Redress - Issue Handling Process
nist63.statement: RPs and CSPs SHALL enable individuals to convey grievances and seek redress through an issue handling process that is documented, accessible, trackable, and usable by all individuals and whose instructions are easy to find on a public-facing website.

nist63.title: KBV
nist63.statement: Knowledge-based verification (KBV) or knowledge-based authentication SHALL NOT be used for identity verification.

nist63.title: Data Washing
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL take measures to prevent unsuccessful applicants from inferring the accuracy of any self-asserted information with that confirmed by authoritative or credible sources.

nist63.title: Protected Channel
nist63.statement: Each online transaction within the identity proofing process, including transactions that involve third parties, SHALL occur over an authenticated, protected channel.

nist63.title: Auto Attack Protections
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL implement automated attack protections for the identity proofing process, such as bot detection, mitigation, and management solutions; behavioral analytics; web application firewall settings; and network traffic analysis.

nist63.title: Invalidate Confirm Code
nist63.statement: Upon its use, the CSP SHALL invalidate the confirmation code.

nist63.title: Continue Code Throttling
nist63.statement: The verification of continuation codes SHALL be subject to throttling requirements, as provided in Sec. 3.2.2 of [SP800-63B].

nist63.title: Invalidate Continue Code
nist63.statement: Upon its use, the CSP SHALL invalidate the continuation code.

nist63.title: Bio Consent
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL obtain explicit informed consent to collect and use biometrics from all applicants.

nist63.title: Reasonable Assurance
nist63.statement: If a CSP collects biometric samples from applicants, it SHALL collect them in a way that provides reasonable assurance that the biometric characteristic is collected from the applicant and not another subject.

nist63.title: MRZ Data
nist63.statement: If a Machine Readable Zone (MRZ) or barcode is present on the evidence, the optical capture and inspection SHALL compare the MRZ data to the printed data on the evidence for consistency.

nist63.title: Live Document Capture
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL implement live capture of documents during the validation process and SHALL implement passive or active document presence checks (also called document liveness).

nist63.title: Analyze Digital Media
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL analyze all digital media submitted during the identity proofing process for artifacts and indicators of potential modification, manipulation, tampering, or forgery.

nist63.title: Applicant Reference Evidence
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL make a list of acceptable evidence of relationship available to the applicant reference prior to initiating the relationship confirmation process.

nist63.title: AR Relationship Evidence
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL request evidence of the applicant's relationship (e.g., notarized power of attorney, a professional certification).

nist63.title: IAL1 Evidence Collection
nist63.statement: For identity proofing at IAL1, the CSP SHALL collect: one piece of FAIR evidence that can be digitally validated or that includes a facial portrait or other biometric; OR, one piece of STRONG evidence; OR, one piece of SUPERIOR evidence.

nist63.title: IAL1 Attribute Collection
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL collect all core attributes, including at least one government identifier.

nist63.title: IAL1 Evidence Validation
nist63.statement: Each piece of evidence presented SHALL be validated using one of the methods [provided in Sec. 4.1.4].

nist63.title: IAL1 Attribute Validation
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL validate all core attributes and the government identifier against an authoritative or credible source to determine accuracy.

nist63.title: IAL1 Verification Requirements
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL verify the applicant's ownership of one piece of evidence using one of the methods [provided in 4.1.6].

nist63.title: IAL1 Remote Attended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For Remote Attended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following further requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL1 On-Site Attended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For On-site Attended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL1 On-Site Unattended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For On-site Unattended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL1 Proofing Notification
nist63.statement: Upon the successful completion of identity proofing at IAL1, the CSP SHALL send a notification of proofing to a validated address for the applicant, as specified in Sec. 3.10.

nist63.title: IAL1 Authenticator Binding
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide the ability for the applicant to bind an authenticator using one of the following methods: (a) Remote enrollment of a subscriber-provided authenticator consistent with the requirements for the authenticator type, as defined in Sec. 4.1.3 of [SP800-63B]. (b) Distribution of a physical authenticator to a validated address. (c) Distribution or on-site enrollment of an authenticator.

nist63.title: IAL1 Subscriber Verification
nist63.statement: If authenticators are bound outside of a single protected session with the user, the CSP SHALL confirm the presence of the intended subscriber through one of the following methods: (a) Return of a continuation code. (b) Comparison against a biometric collected at the time of proofing.

nist63.title: IAL2 Evidence Collection
nist63.statement: For identity proofing at IAL2, the CSP SHALL collect: one piece of FAIR evidence and one piece of STRONG evidence; OR, two pieces of STRONG evidence; OR, one piece of SUPERIOR evidence.

nist63.title: IAL2 Attribute Collection
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL collect all core attributes, including at least one government identifier. Validated evidence is the preferred source of identity attributes.

nist63.title: IAL2 Fair/Strong Validation
nist63.statement: Each piece of FAIR or STRONG evidence that is presented SHALL be validated using one of the following techniques: (a) Confirming the authenticity of the digital evidence by interrogating the digital security features (e.g., signatures on assertions or data). (b) Confirming the authenticity of the physical evidence using automated scanning technology that can detect physical security features. (c) Confirming the integrity of any physical security features through a visual inspection by a proofing agent using a real-time or asynchronous process (e.g., offline manual review). (d) Confirming the integrity of any physical security features through physical and tactile inspection by a proofing agent at an on-site location.

nist63.title: IAL2 Superior Validation
nist63.statement: Each piece of SUPERIOR evidence SHALL be validated through the cryptographic verification of the evidence contents and the issuing source, including digital signature verification and the validation of any trust chain back to a trust anchor.

nist63.title: IAL2 Attribute Validation
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL validate all core attributes by either: (a) Comparing the government identifier and other core attributes against an authoritative or credible source to determine accuracy. (b) Validating the accuracy of digitally signed attributes that are contained on SUPERIOR evidence through the public key of the issuing source.

nist63.title: IAL2 Remote Attended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For Remote Attended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL2 On-Site Attended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For On-site Attended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL2 On-Site Unattended Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For On-site Unattended identity proofing, if the CSP records a video session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL2 Proofing Notification
nist63.statement: Upon the successful completion of identity proofing at IAL2, the CSP SHALL send a notification of proofing to a validated address for the applicant, as specified in Sec. 3.10.

nist63.title: IAL2 Authenticator Binding
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide the ability for the applicant to bind an authenticator using one of the following methods: (a) Remote enrollment of a subscriber-provided authenticator consistent with the requirements for the authenticator type, as defined in Sec. 4.1.3 of [SP800-63B]. (b) Distribution of a physical authenticator to a validated address. (c) Distribution or on-site enrollment of an authenticator.

nist63.title: IAL2 Subscriber Verification
nist63.statement: If authenticators are bound outside of a single protected session with the user, the CSP SHALL confirm the presence of the intended subscriber through one of the following methods: (a) Return of a continuation code. (b) Comparison against a biometric collected at the time of proofing.

nist63.title: IAL3 Evidence Collection
nist63.statement: For identity proofing at IAL3, the CSP SHALL collect: one piece of FAIR evidence and one piece of STRONG evidence; OR, two pieces of STRONG evidence; OR one piece of SUPERIOR evidence.

nist63.title: IAL3 Attribute Collection
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL collect all core attributes, including at least one government identifier.

nist63.title: IAL3 Fair Strong
nist63.statement: Each piece of FAIR or STRONG evidence that is presented SHALL be validated using one of the following techniques: (a) Confirming the authenticity of the digital evidence by interrogating the digital security features (e.g., signatures on assertions or data). (b) Confirming the authenticity of the physical evidence using automated scanning technology that can detect physical security features. (c) Confirming the integrity of any physical security features through a visual inspection by a proofing agent using a real-time or asynchronous process (e.g., offline manual review).

nist63.title: IAL3 Superior Evidence
nist63.statement: Each piece of SUPERIOR evidence SHALL be validated through the cryptographic verification of the evidence contents and the issuing source, including digital signature verification and the validation of any trust chain back to a trust anchor.

nist63.title: IAL3 ID Verification
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL verify the applicant's ownership of the strongest piece of evidence (STRONG or SUPERIOR) by one of the following methods: (a) Confirming the applicant's ability to successfully authenticate to a physical device or application (e.g., a mobile driver's license) and comparing a digitally protected and transmitted facial portrait to the applicant. (b) Comparing the applicant's facial image to the facial portrait on the presented evidence via an automated comparison. (c) Visually comparing the applicant's facial image to the facial portrait on the presented evidence during an on-site attended session or a remote attended session. (d) Performing an automated comparison of a stored biometric on the identity evidence or in the authoritative records associated with the evidence to a sample provided by the applicant.

nist63.title: IAL3 Recorded Video
nist63.statement: For on-site attended identity proofing with collocated agents, if the CSP records a session, the following additional requirements apply: (a) The CSP SHALL notify the applicant of the recording prior to initiating a recorded session. (b) The CSP SHALL gain consent from the applicant prior to initiating a recorded session. (c) The CSP SHALL publish their retention schedule and deletion processes for all video records.

nist63.title: IAL3 Proofing Notification
nist63.statement: Upon the successful completion of identity proofing at IAL3, the CSP SHALL send a notification of proofing to a validated address for the applicant, as specified in Sec. 3.10.

nist63.title: IAL3 Subscriber Verification
nist63.statement: If the CSP distributes or enrolls the initial authenticator outside of a single authenticated protected session with the subscriber, the CSP SHALL compare a biometric sample collected from the subscriber to the one collected at the time of proofing prior to registration of the authenticator.

nist63.title: Subscriber Account Access
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide the capability for subscribers to authenticate and access information in their subscriber account.

nist63.title: Subscriber Account AAL
nist63.statement: For subscriber accounts that contain personal information, this capability SHALL be accomplished through AAL2 or AAL3 authentication processes using authenticators that are registered to the subscriber account.

nist63.title: SA Update Requests
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide the capability for a subscriber to request that information be updated in their subscriber account.

nist63.title: SA Update Notifications
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL notify the subscriber of any updates made to information in the subscriber account.

nist63.title: Subscriber Account Compromise
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide the capability for the subscriber to report any unauthorized access or potential compromise to information in their subscriber account.

nist63.title: AAL Minimum Requirements
nist63.statement: To satisfy the requirements of a given AAL and be recognized as a subscriber, a claimant SHALL authenticate to an RP (or IdP, as described in [SP800-63C]) with a process whose strength is equal to or greater than the requirements at that level.

nist63.title: Personal Information AAL
nist63.statement: Federal agencies SHALL select a minimum of AAL2 when personal information is made available online.

nist63.title: AAL1 Authenticator Types
nist63.statement: AAL1 authentication SHALL use any of the following authentication types, which are further defined in Sec. 3: (a) Password (Sec. 3.1.1): A memorizable secret typically chosen by the subscriber. (b) Look-up secret (Sec. 3.1.2): A secret determined by the claimant by looking up a prompted value in a list held by the subscriber. (c) Out-of-band device (Sec. 3.1.3): A secret sent or received through a separate communication channel with the subscriber. (d) Single-factor one-time password (OTP) (Sec. 3.1.4): A one-time secret obtained from a device or application held by the subscriber. (e) Multi-factor OTP (Sec. 3.1.5): A one-time secret obtained from a device or application held by the subscriber that requires activation by a second authentication factor. (f) Single-factor cryptographic authentication (Sec. 3.1.6): Proof of possession and control via an authentication protocol of a cryptographic key held by the subscriber. (g) Multi-factor cryptographic authentication (Sec. 3.1.7): Proof of possession and control via an authentication protocol of a cryptographic key held by the subscriber that requires activation by a second authentication factor.

nist63.title: AAL1 Approved Cryptography
nist63.statement: Authenticators used at AAL1 SHALL use approved cryptography.

nist63.title: AAL1 Authenticated Protected Channels
nist63.statement: Communication between the claimant and verifier SHALL occur via one or more authenticated protected channels.

nist63.title: AAL1 Overall Timeout
nist63.statement: A definite reauthentication overall timeout SHALL be established, which SHOULD be no more than 30 days at AAL1.

nist63.title: AAL2 Multiple Factors
nist63.statement: At AAL2, authentication SHALL use either a multi-factor authenticator (MFA) or a combination of two separate authentication factors.

nist63.title: AAL2 Approved Cryptography
nist63.statement: Authenticators used at AAL2 SHALL use approved cryptography.

nist63.title: AAL2 Replay Resistance
nist63.statement: At least one authenticator used at AAL2 SHALL be replay-resistant, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

nist63.title: AAL2 Authenticated Protected Channels
nist63.statement: Communication between the claimant and verifier SHALL occur via one or more authenticated protected channels.

nist63.title: AAL2 Phishing Resistance Offer
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL offer at least one phishing-resistant authentication option at AAL2, as described in Sec. 3.2.5.

nist63.title: AAL2 Phishing Resistance Requirement
nist63.statement: Federal agencies SHALL require their staff, contractors, and partners to use phishing-resistant authentication to access federal information systems.

nist63.title: AAL2 Reauthentication
nist63.statement: Periodic reauthentication of subscriber sessions SHALL be performed, as described in Sec. 5.2.

nist63.title: AAL3 Authenticator Combinations
nist63.statement: AAL3 authentication SHALL require an authenticator combination consisting of either multi-factor cryptographic authentication (Sec. 3.1.7); or single-factor cryptographic authentication (Sec. 3.1.6) used in conjunction with either a password (Sec. 3.1.1) or a biometric comparison.

nist63.title: AAL3 Phishing Resistance
nist63.statement: The cryptographic authenticator used at AAL3 SHALL provide phishing resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.5.

nist63.title: AAL3 Reauthentication
nist63.statement: Periodic reauthentication of subscriber sessions SHALL be performed, as described in Sec. 5.2.

nist63.title: Redress Provision
nist63.statement: The verifier and associated CSP or IdP SHALL provide mechanisms for the redress of subscriber complaints and problems that arise from subscriber authentication processes, as described in Sec. 5.6 of [SP800-63].

nist63.title: Redress Usability
nist63.statement: These mechanisms SHALL be easy for subscribers to find and use.

nist63.title: Password Choice
nist63.statement: Passwords SHALL either be chosen by the subscriber or assigned randomly by the CSP.

nist63.title: Password Blocklist
nist63.statement: If the CSP disallows a chosen password because it is on a blocklist of commonly used, expected, or compromised values (see Sec. 3.1.1.2), the subscriber SHALL be required to choose a different password.

nist63.title: Password Composition
nist63.statement: Other composition requirements for passwords SHALL NOT be imposed.

nist63.title: Password Length
nist63.statement: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length. Verifiers and CSPs MAY allow passwords that are only used as part of multi-factor authentication processes to be shorter but SHALL require them to be a minimum of eight characters in length.

nist63.title: Unicode Passwords
nist63.statement: Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD accept Unicode [ISO/IEC 10646] characters in passwords. Each Unicode code point SHALL be counted as a single character when evaluating password length.

nist63.title: Password Hints
nist63.statement: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT permit the subscriber to store a hint (e.g., a reminder of how the password was created) that is accessible to an unauthenticated claimant.

nist63.title: Passwords Not KBA
nist63.statement: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT prompt subscribers to use knowledge-based authentication (KBA) (e.g., "What was the name of your first pet?") or security questions when choosing passwords.

nist63.title: Password Full Verification
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL request the password to be provided in full (not a subset of it) and SHALL verify the entire submitted password (e.g., not truncate it).

nist63.title: Password Verifier Blocklist
nist63.statement: When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords.

nist63.title: Verifier Blocklist Substrings
nist63.statement: The entire password SHALL be subject to comparison, not substrings or words that might be contained therein.

nist63.title: Verifier Blocklist Response
nist63.statement: If the chosen password is found on the blocklist, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to select a different secret and SHALL provide the reason for rejection.

nist63.title: Strong Password Guidance
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL offer guidance to the subscriber to help the subscriber choose a strong password. This is particularly important following the rejection of a password on the blocklist as it discourages trivial modifications of listed weak passwords [Blocklists].

nist63.title: Password Rate-Limiting
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: Password Manager Use
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL allow the use of password managers and autofill functionality.

nist63.title: Password Authenticated Protected Channels
nist63.statement: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when requesting passwords.

nist63.title: Online Look-Up Secret Delivery
nist63.statement: If delivered via an online session, the session SHALL be authenticated by the subscriber at AAL2 or higher and SHALL deliver the secrets through an authenticated protected channel and in accordance with the post-enrollment binding requirements in Sec. 4.1.2.

nist63.title: Look-Up Secret Prompt
nist63.statement: Verifiers of look-up secrets SHALL prompt the claimant for a secret from their authenticator.

nist63.title: Look-Up Secret Reuse
nist63.statement: A secret from a look-up secret authenticator SHALL be used successfully only once.

nist63.title: Look-Up Secret Rate Limiting
nist63.statement: The verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Channel Independence
nist63.statement: The out-of-band authenticator SHALL establish a separate channel with the verifier to retrieve the out-of-band secret or authentication request.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Approved Encryption
nist63.statement: Communication over the secondary channel SHALL use approved encryption unless sent via the public switched telephone network (PSTN).

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Email Prohibition
nist63.statement: Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication because it may be vulnerable to: (a) Access using only a password. (b) Interception in transit or at intermediate mail servers. (c) Rerouting attacks, such as those caused by Domain Name System (DNS) spoofing.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Secondary Approval
nist63.statement: If the out-of-band authenticator requests approval over the secondary communication channel rather than by presenting a secret that the claimant transfers to the primary communication channel, it SHALL accept a transfer of the secret from the primary channel and send it to the verifier over the secondary channel to associate the approval with the authentication transaction.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Transfer Methods
nist63.statement: Depending on the type of out-of-band authenticator, one of the following SHALL take place: (a) Transfer of the secret from the secondary to the primary channel. As shown in Fig. 1, the verifier MAY signal the device that contains the subscriber's authenticator to indicate a readiness to authenticate. It SHALL then transmit a random secret to the out-of-band authenticator and wait for the secret to be returned via the primary communication channel. (b) Transfer of the secret from the primary to the secondary channel. As shown in Fig. 2, the verifier SHALL transmit a random authentication secret to the claimant via the primary channel. It SHALL then wait for the secret to be returned via the secondary channel from the claimant's out-of-band authenticator. The verifier MAY additionally display an address, such as a phone number or VoIP address, for the claimant to use in addressing its response to the verifier.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Time Limit
nist63.statement: In all cases, the authentication SHALL be considered invalid unless completed within 10 minutes.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Replay Resistance
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL accept a given authentication secret as valid only once during the validity period to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Rate Limiting
nist63.statement: If the authentication secret is less than 64 bits long, the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the total number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: Out-Of-Band Failure Count
nist63.statement: Generating a new authentication secret SHALL NOT reset the failed authentication count.

nist63.title: Pstn Modification Binding
nist63.statement: Setting or changing the pre-registered telephone number is considered to be the binding of a new authenticator and SHALL only occur as described in Sec. 4.1.2.

nist63.title: MF-OOB Activation
nist63.statement: Each use of the authenticator SHALL require the presentation of the activation factor.

nist63.title: TOTP Change Frequency
nist63.statement: If the nonce used to generate the authenticator output is based on a real-time clock, the nonce SHALL be changed at least once every two minutes.

nist63.title: OTP Replay Protection
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL accept a given OTP only once while it is valid to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

nist63.title: OTP Rate Limiting
nist63.statement: The verifier SHOULD implement or, if the authenticator output is less than 64 bits in length, SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: MF-OTP Activation
nist63.statement: Each use of the authenticator SHALL require the input of the activation factor.

nist63.title: MF-TOTP Change Frequency
nist63.statement: If the nonce used to generate the authenticator output is based on a real-time clock, the nonce SHALL be changed at least once every two minutes.

nist63.title: MF-OTP Replay Protection
nist63.statement: Verifiers SHALL accept a given OTP only once while it is valid to provide replay resistance, as described in Sec. 3.2.7.

nist63.title: MF-OTP Rate Limiting
nist63.statement: The verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as required by Sec. 3.2.10.

nist63.title: MF Crypto Activation
nist63.statement: Each authentication event SHALL require input and verification of the local activation factor.

nist63.title: Physical Authenticator Instructions
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL provide subscriber instructions for appropriately protecting the authenticator against theft or loss.

nist63.title: Physical Authenticator Invalidation
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide a mechanism to invalidate the authenticator immediately upon notification from a subscriber that the authenticator's loss, theft, or compromise is suspected.

nist63.title: Rate Limiting Upper Bound
nist63.statement: Unless otherwise specified in the description of a given authenticator, the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts using a specific authenticator on a single subscriber account to no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator.

nist63.title: Rate Limiting Authenticator Association
nist63.statement: If more than one authenticator is involved with an excessive number of authentication attempts (e.g., single-factor cryptographic authenticator and centrally verified password), both authenticators SHALL be disabled.

nist63.title: Rate Limiting Rebinding
nist63.statement: Authenticators that have been disabled SHALL be required to rebind to the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 4.1, to be usable in the future.

nist63.title: Rate Limiting AAL Limitation
nist63.statement: If the retry count of an authenticator is reset following a successful authentication, the maximum AAL of the authenticator being reset SHALL not exceed the AAL of the session from which it is being reset.

nist63.title: Biometrics Applicability
nist63.statement: Biometrics SHALL only be used as part of multi-factor authentication with a physical authenticator (i.e., "something you have").

nist63.title: Biometrics Not Cached
nist63.statement: The biometric characteristic SHALL be presented and compared for each authentication operation.

nist63.title: Biometrics Alternatives
nist63.statement: An alternative nonbiometric authentication option SHALL always be provided to the subscriber.

nist63.title: Biometric Pad
nist63.statement: The biometric system SHOULD implement PAD for iris and fingerprint modalities and SHALL implement PAD for facial recognition.

nist63.title: Biometric Voice Prohibition
nist63.statement: Biometric comparison based on voice SHALL NOT be used.

nist63.title: Biometric Failure Threshold
nist63.statement: The biometric system SHALL allow no more than five consecutive failed authentication attempts or 10 consecutive failed attempts if PAD is implemented and meets the above requirements.

nist63.title: Biometric Failure Delay
nist63.statement: Once that limit has been reached, the biometric authenticator SHALL impose a delay of at least 30 seconds before each subsequent attempt with an overall limit of no more than 50 consecutive failed authentication attempts or 100 if PAD is implemented due to the mitigation of presentation attacks.

nist63.title: Biometric Failure Limit
nist63.statement: Once the overall limit is reached, the biometric system SHALL disable biometric authentication and offer another factor (e.g., a different biometric modality or an activation secret if it is not a required factor) if such an alternative method is already available.

nist63.title: Biometric Unlocking Independence
nist63.statement: The presentation of a biometric factor for authenticator activation SHALL be a separate operation from unlocking the host device (e.g., smartphone).

nist63.title: Phishing Resistance Manual Prohibition
nist63.statement: Authenticators that involve the manual entry of an authenticator output (e.g., out-of-band and OTP authenticators) SHALL NOT be considered phishing-resistant because the manual entry does not bind the authenticator output to the specific session being authenticated.

nist63.title: Channel Binding Authenticated Protected Channel
nist63.statement: An authentication protocol with channel binding SHALL establish an authenticated protected channel with the verifier.

nist63.title: Channel Binding Identifier
nist63.statement: The protocol SHALL then strongly and irreversibly bind a channel identifier negotiated in establishing the authenticated protected channel to the authenticator output (e.g., by signing the two values together using a private key controlled by the claimant for which the public key is known to the verifier).

nist63.title: Channel Binding Validation
nist63.statement: The verifier SHALL validate the signature or other information used to prove phishing resistance.

nist63.title: Name Binding Authenticated Protected Channel
nist63.statement: An authentication protocol with verifier name binding SHALL establish an authenticated protected channel with the verifier.

nist63.title: Name Binding Authenticated Verifier
nist63.statement: The protocol SHALL generate an authenticator output that is cryptographically bound to a verifier identifier that is authenticated as part of the protocol.

nist63.title: Intent Requirement
nist63.statement: The authenticator itself SHALL establish authentication intent.

nist63.title: Intent Explicit
nist63.statement: In scenarios involving biometric authentication not requiring claimant action, an explicit mechanism (e.g., tapping a software or physical button) SHALL be provided to establish authentication intent.

nist63.title: Activation Secret Minimum Length
nist63.statement: Authenticators that use activation secrets SHALL require the secrets to be at least four characters in length and SHOULD require the secrets to be at least six characters in length.

nist63.title: Activation Secret Retry Limit
nist63.statement: The authenticator or verifier SHALL implement a retry-limiting mechanism that limits the number of consecutive failed activation attempts using the authenticator to no more than 10.

nist63.title: Retry Limit Authenticator Implementation
nist63.statement: Unless the authenticator generates an invalid output when an incorrect activation secret is provided, retry limiting SHALL be implemented in the authenticator.

nist63.title: Activation Secret Independence
nist63.statement: Submitting the activation factor SHALL be a separate operation from unlocking the host device (e.g., smartphone).

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Physical Proximity Requirement
nist63.statement: To minimize the attack surface for threats to the authenticator-endpoint connection, the authentication process SHALL require physical proximity between the authenticator and endpoint by establishing a wireless connection with a range of no more than 240 meters.

nist63.title: Wireless  Authenticator Key Establishment
nist63.statement: Wireless connections SHALL establish a key for encrypted communication between the authenticator and endpoint in one of the following ways: (1) Through a temporary wired connection between the devices. (2) Through an association process that is similar to a pairing process but does not require a persistent relationship between devices to establish a key for encrypted communication between the authenticator and endpoint.

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Pairing Code
nist63.statement: If an association process is used, it SHALL employ a pairing code or other shared secret between the devices.

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Pairing Code Length
nist63.statement: If an association process is used, either the authenticator or endpoint SHALL have a pairing code that is at least six decimal digits (or equivalent) in length that MAY be printed on the device.

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Association Methods
nist63.statement: If an association process is used, the pairing code SHALL be conveyed between the devices by manual entry or using a QR code or similar representation that is optically communicated.

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Pairing Code Use
nist63.statement: A pairing code SHALL be used if the authenticator is configured to require authenticated pairing.

nist63.title: Wireless Authenticator Persistent Key Removal
nist63.statement: A mechanism for endpoints to remove persistent keys SHALL be provided.

nist63.title: Hybrid Connection Establishment
nist63.statement: Hybrid connections (e.g., hybrid transports specified by the CTAP2.2 protocol) SHALL be established between authenticators and endpoints in one of the following ways: (1) By communicating initial keying information and the identity of the tunnel service to be used via a displayed QR code or similar visual representation coupled with the receipt by the endpoint of wireless data containing the additional information required to establish the tunnel connection. (2) Through cached keying and tunnel information retained by the authenticator and endpoint from a previous authentication transaction.

nist63.title: Hybrid Connection Proximity
nist63.statement: The wireless data SHALL be conveyed over a technology with a maximum effective range of no more than 240 meters.

nist63.title: Hybrid Connection Association Removal
nist63.statement: A mechanism for endpoints to remove cached associations with authenticators SHALL be provided.

nist63.title: Multiple Authenticator Binding
nist63.statement: Accordingly, CSPs SHALL permit the binding of multiple authenticators to a subscriber account.

nist63.title: Binding Authentication Requirement
nist63.statement: When any new authenticator is bound to a subscriber account, the CSP SHALL ensure that the process requires authentication at either the maximum AAL currently available in the subscriber account or the maximum AAL at which the new authenticator will be used, whichever is lower.

nist63.title: Binding Notification Requirement
nist63.statement: When an authenticator is added, the CSP SHALL notify the subscriber via a mechanism independent of the transaction binding the new authenticator, as described in Sec. 4.6.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Binding
nist63.statement: The binding process SHALL proceed in one of the following ways: (1) An endpoint that has authenticated to the CSP requests a binding code from the CSP. The binding code is input into the endpoint associated with the new authenticator and sent to the CSP. (2) The endpoint associated with the new authenticator obtains a binding code from the CSP. The binding code is input to an authenticated endpoint and sent to the CSP.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Identifier Binding Code Length
nist63.statement: The binding code SHALL be at least 40 bits in length if it is used with an identifier entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Non-Identifier Binding Code Length
nist63.statement: The binding code SHALL be at least 112 bits in length if it is not used with an identifier entered by the subscriber on the new authenticator.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Association Methods
nist63.statement: When binding an external authenticator, the subscriber SHALL transfer the binding code to the other endpoint manually or via a local out-of-band method such as a QR code.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Binding Code Security
nist63.statement: The binding code SHALL NOT be communicated over an insecure channel.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Binding Code Replay
nist63.statement: When binding an external authenticator, the binding code SHALL be usable only once.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Binding Code Lifetime
nist63.statement: The binding code SHALL be valid for a maximum of 10 minutes.

nist63.title: External Authenticator Binding Instructions
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide clear instructions on what the subscriber should do in the event of an authenticator binding mishap.

nist63.title: Saved Recovery Code Issuance Notification
nist63.statement: The issuance of a replacement recovery code SHALL result in an account recovery notification, as described in Sec. 4.6.

nist63.title: Saved Recovery Code Rate Limitation
nist63.statement: The verification of saved recovery codes SHALL be subject to the throttling requirements in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: Saved Recovery Code Replay
nist63.statement: Following the use of a saved recovery code, the CSP SHALL invalidate that recovery code and SHALL issue a new saved recovery code to the subscriber.

nist63.title: Issued Recovery Code Rate Limitation
nist63.statement: The verification of issued recovery codes SHALL be subject to the throttling requirements in Sec. 3.2.2.

nist63.title: Issued Recovery Code Address Verification Procedure
nist63.statement: To verify an address, the CSP SHALL send a confirmation code with the same characteristics as a recovery code to the newly established recovery address and require that the subscriber return the same confirmation code to the CSP.

nist63.title: Issued Recovery Code Multiple Address Requirement
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL allow the subscriber to establish at least two recovery addresses.

nist63.title: Recovery Contact Addresses
nist63.statement: CSPs that support the use of recovery contacts SHALL allow the subscriber to specify one or more addresses of trusted associates to receive issued recovery codes.

nist63.title: Recovery Contact Management
nist63.statement: If the CSP supports the use of recovery contacts, the CSP SHALL provide methods for subscribers to view and manage recovery contacts.

nist63.title: AAL2 Recovery Requirements
nist63.statement: To recover an account that can authenticate at a maximum of AAL2, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to complete one of the following: (1) Two recovery codes obtained using different methods from the set (i.e., saved, issued, and recovery contacts). (2) One recovery code from the set (i.e., saved, issued, and recovery contacts) plus authentication with a single-factor authenticator that is bound to the subscriber account. (3) Repeated identity proofing (provided that the subscriber account has been identity-proofed).

nist63.title: Account Recovery Notification
nist63.statement: In all cases, account recovery SHALL cause a notification to be sent to the subscriber or their designee, as described in Sec. 4.6.

nist63.title: Expired Authenticators Unusable
nist63.statement: When an authenticator expires, it SHALL NOT be usable for authentication.

nist63.title: Notification Multiple Address Support
nist63.statement: CSPs SHALL support at least two notification addresses per subscriber account.

nist63.title: Notification Address Validation
nist63.statement: For subscriber accounts that have undergone identity proofing, at least one address SHALL have been validated during the identity proofing process.

nist63.title: Notification Multiplicity
nist63.statement: Notifications SHALL be sent to all notification addresses except postal addresses.

nist63.title: Postal Notification
nist63.statement: However, notifications SHALL be sent to postal addresses if no other form of notification address is stored in the subscriber account or if the notification is for account recovery at AAL3.

nist63.title: Postal Recovery Notification
nist63.statement: Account recovery notifications SHALL also be sent to a postal address if the only other notification address in the subscriber account is the address to which an issued recovery code was sent.

nist63.title: Session AAL Limitation
nist63.statement: A session MAY be considered at a lower AAL than the authentication event but SHALL NOT be considered at a higher AAL than the authentication event.

nist63.title: Session Transport Security Maintenance
nist63.statement: Following authentication, authenticated sessions SHALL NOT fall back to an insecure transport (e.g., from https to http).

nist63.title: Access Tokens Not Presence
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL NOT interpret the presence of an access token as an indicator of the subscriber's presence in the absence of other signals.

nist63.title: Syncable Key Management
nist63.statement: Authenticators that enable the use of syncable authentication keys SHOULD provide a user interface (UI) that allows subscribers to view the services for which they have created a syncable authentication key, whether that key has been synced, and where that key has been synced. The UI SHALL NOT expose the authentication key itself.

nist63.title: Approved Cryptography: Assertion Signatures
nist63.statement: At FAL1, the IdP SHALL sign the assertion using approved cryptography.

nist63.title: Signature Verification
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL validate the signature using the verification key associated with the expected IdP.

nist63.title: FAL1 RP Assertion Replay Protection
nist63.statement: Each RP in the [assertion] audience SHALL enforce replay protection mechanisms in the assertion to ensure that the same assertion is not accepted by a given RP multiple times.

nist63.title: RP-Initiated Transactions
nist63.statement: The federation transaction SHALL be initiated by the RP.

nist63.title: Federated Identifier Privacy Protection
nist63.statement: At FAL2, federated identifiers SHALL NOT contain plaintext personal information, such as usernames, email addresses, employee numbers, etc.

nist63.title: xAL Reporting
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL always indicate the resulting xAL in the assertion, even if the request has not been met.

nist63.title: IAL Reporting
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL inform the RP of the following information for each federation transaction: The IAL of the subscriber account being presented to the RP, or an indication that no IAL claim is being made.

nist63.title: AAL Reporting
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL inform the RP of the following information for each federation transaction: The AAL of the currently active session of the subscriber at the IdP, or an indication that no AAL claim is being made.

nist63.title: FAL Reporting
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL inform the RP of the following information for each federation transaction: The FAL of the federation transaction.

nist63.title: xAL Requirements
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL determine the minimum IAL, AAL, and FAL that it is willing to accept for access to any offered functionality and assess all IdP assertions to ensure that these xALs have been met before granting access to protected resources.

nist63.title: Unmet xAL Requirements
nist63.statement: If IdP responses do not meet the requested parameters, the RP SHALL have a mechanism for addressing these requests (e.g., declining the request or routing the user to an exception handling process).

nist63.title: Proxy FAL Accuracy
nist63.statement: The FAL of the connection between the proxy and the downstream RP is considered to be the lowest FAL along the entire path, and the proxy SHALL accurately represent this to the downstream RP.

nist63.title: Proxy Identifier
nist63.statement: The federated identifier (see Sec. 3.4) of an assertion from a proxy SHALL indicate the proxy as the issuer of the assertion.

nist63.title: PPI Uniqueness
nist63.statement: When using pairwise pseudonymous identifiers within the assertions generated by the IdP for the RP, the IdP SHALL generate a different federated identifier for each RP (see Sec. 3.4.1.2) or set of RPs (see Sec. 3.4.1.3).

nist63.title: Anonymous PPIs
nist63.statement: The PPI SHALL contain no identifying information about the subscriber (e.g., username, email address, employee number).

nist63.title: Redress Coordination
nist63.statement: Trust agreements SHALL define necessary mechanisms and materials to coordinate redress and issues between the different participants in the federation, as discussed in Sec. 3.5.3.

nist63.title: Subscriber Disclosure
nist63.statement: As such, the relevant terms of the trust agreement SHALL be made available to subscribers in clear and understandable language.

nist63.title: MTA Vetting: IdP Assertions
nist63.statement: The vetting of CSPs, IdPs, and RPs SHALL establish that: (4) The assertions generated by IdPs adhere to the requirements in Sec. 4.9 or Sec. 5.8, as applicable.

nist63.title: RP Subscriber Redress
nist63.statement: For matters that involve the RP subscriber account (including any attributes stored in the account), RP functionality, bound authenticators, RP allowlists, and other items under the RP's control, the RP SHALL provide a clear and accessible means of redress to the subscriber.

nist63.title: RP Redress Routing
nist63.statement: For matters that involve the IdP or CSP, the RP SHALL provide the subscriber with a means of initiating the redress process with the IdP or CSP, as appropriate.

nist63.title: IdP Subscriber Redress
nist63.statement: For matters that involve the use of the subscriber account in federation transactions, including attribute values and derived attribute values made available over federation transactions, IdP functionality, holder-of-key authenticators, IdP allowlists, and other items in the IdP's control, the IdP SHALL provide a clear and accessible means of redress to the subscriber.

nist63.title: IdP Redress Routing: RP
nist63.statement: For matters that also involve a particular RP, the IdP SHALL provide the subscriber with a means of initiating the redress process with the RP.

nist63.title: IdP Redress Routing: CSP
nist63.statement: For matters that involve a subscriber account that has been made available to the IdP, the IdP SHALL provide the subscriber with a means of initiating the redress process with the CSP.

nist63.title: CSP Redress
nist63.statement: For matters that involve the subscriber account, including identity attributes and authenticators in the subscriber account, the CSP SHALL provide the subscriber with a clear and accessible means of redress.

nist63.title: Secure Key Exchange
nist63.statement: Protocols that require the transfer of cryptographic key information SHALL use an authenticated protected channel to exchange the cryptographic key information needed to operate the federated relationship, including any shared secrets or public keys.

nist63.title: Wildcard Identifier Prohibition
nist63.statement: When domain names, URIs, or other structured identifiers are used to identify parties, wildcards SHALL NOT be used.

nist63.title: Key Rotation Security
nist63.statement: The allowable update process for any identifiers and cryptographic keys... SHALL be executed using an authenticated protected channel, as in the initial cryptographic key establishment.

nist63.title: Software Attestation Validation
nist63.statement: When attestations are required by the trust agreement or requested as part of the federation protocol, received attestations SHALL be validated by the receiver.

nist63.title: RP Subscriber Account Termination Data Removal
nist63.statement: Termination SHALL include the removal of all federated identifiers, bound authenticators, attributes, and identity information associated with the account, in accordance with Sec. 3.11.3.

nist63.title: Federated Identifier Change Notifications
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL provide a notice to the subscriber when: (a) A new federated identifier is added to an existing RP subscriber account, or (b) A federated identifier is removed from an RP subscriber account, but the account is not terminated.

nist63.title: Termination Notice Consideration
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL consider the reason for termination when determining whether to send a notice to the subscriber, as discussed in Sec. 5.4 of [SP800-63A].

nist63.title: Account Linking Authentication Requirement
nist63.statement: If the RP allows a subscriber to link multiple subscriber accounts..., the RP SHALL require an authenticated session with the subscriber account for all linking functions.

nist63.title: Removed Federated Identifier Access Prohibition
nist63.statement: When a federated identifier is removed from an RP subscriber account, the RP SHALL disallow access to the RP subscriber account from the removed federated identifier.

nist63.title: Account Resolution Attribute Sufficiency
nist63.statement: An RP that performs account resolution SHALL ensure that the attributes requested from the IdP are sufficient to uniquely resolve the subscriber within the RP's system before linking the federated identifier with the RP subscriber account and granting access.

nist63.title: RP Authenticated Session Requirements
nist63.statement: An authenticated session SHALL be created by the RP only when the following conditions are true: (a) The RP has processed and verified a valid assertion. (b) The assertion is from the expected IdP for a transaction. (c) The IdP that issued the assertion is the IdP identified in the federated identifier of the assertion. (d) The assertion is associated with an RP subscriber account, which may be ephemeral. (e) The RP subscriber account has been provisioned at the RP through the method specified in the trust agreement.

nist63.title: RP Authenticated Session Requirements: HoK Verification
nist63.statement: If the assertion is a holder-of-key assertion at FAL3, the authenticator indicated in the assertion SHALL be verified before the RP subscriber account is associated with an authenticated session, as discussed in Sec. 3.15.

nist63.title: Subscriber Account Deprovisioning via API
nist63.statement: To prevent RP retention of identity attributes for accounts that have been terminated at the IdP, the IdP SHALL use the provisioning API to deprovision RP subscriber accounts for terminated subscriber accounts except where restricted by RP data retention requirements, policies, or regulation.

nist63.title: IdP Data Exchange Minimization
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL limit the transmission of subscriber information to only that which is necessary for the system to function and is stipulated and disclosed by the trust agreement.

nist63.title: Prohibition on Coerced Consent
nist63.statement: When an IdP gathers the subscriber's consent to use information outside the identity transaction, the IdP SHALL NOT make consent for the additional processing a condition of the identity service.

nist63.title: Subscriber Notice & Consent for Additional Uses
nist63.statement: If an RP uses the subscriber's identity information for any purpose other than those stipulated in the trust agreement, the RP SHALL inform the subscriber and obtain their consent for such additional uses.

nist63.title: Attribute Bundle Signature Validation
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL validate the signature specific to the attribute bundle as well as any container signatures, such as the signature of the assertion as a whole.

nist63.title: Bundle-Embedded IdP Verification Key Validation
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL confirm that the assertion is presented by the identity claimed in the attribute bundle by verifying the signature over the assertion using the IdP's verification key in the signed attribute bundle.

nist63.title: Derived Attribute Value Non-Disclosure
nist63.statement: To preserve privacy, derived attribute values SHALL NOT disclose the underlying attribute value to a requester.

nist63.title: Identity API Access Insufficient for Session Establishment
nist63.statement: Since the time limitation is separate from the validity time window of the assertion and the lifetime of the authenticated session at the RP, access to an identity API by the RP without an associated valid assertion SHALL NOT be sufficient for the establishment of an authenticated session at the RP.

nist63.title: Identity API Transaction Scope
nist63.statement: When access to the identity API is granted within the context of a federation transaction, the attributes provided by an identity API SHALL be associated with only the single subscriber identified in the associated assertion.

nist63.title: Identity API Subject Identifier Inclusion
nist63.statement: If the identity API is hosted by the IdP, the returned attributes SHALL include the subject identifier for the subscriber.

nist63.title: Assertion Uniqueness
nist63.statement: Assertions SHALL be sufficiently unique to permit unique identification by the target RP.

nist63.title: Signed Assertions
nist63.statement: Assertions SHALL be cryptographically signed by the issuer (IdP).

nist63.title: Signature Coverage
nist63.statement: This signature SHALL cover the entire assertion, including its identifier, issuer, audience, subject, and time validity window.

nist63.title: Signature Mechanisms
nist63.statement: The assertion signature SHALL either be a digital signature using asymmetric keys or a MAC using a symmetric key that is shared between the RP and issuer with approved cryptography.

nist63.title: Encryption
nist63.statement: When encrypting assertions, the IdP SHALL encrypt the contents of the assertion using the RP's encryption key with approved cryptography.

nist63.title: Assertion Audience Restriction
nist63.statement: Assertions SHALL use audience restriction techniques to allow an RP to recognize whether it is the intended target of an issued assertion.

nist63.title: RP Audience Validation
nist63.statement: All RPs SHALL check that the audience of an assertion contains an identifier for their RP to prevent the assertion injection and replay of an assertion generated for one RP at another RP.

nist63.title: HoK Authenticator Identifier
nist63.statement: A holder-of-key assertion (Fig. 3) SHALL include a unique identifier for an authenticator that can be verified independently by the RP, such as the public key of a certificate controlled by the subscriber.

nist63.title: HoK Validation
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL verify that the subscriber possesses the authenticator identified by the assertion. Holder-of-key assertions are most often used when the authenticator technology is tied to a public-key infrastructure (PKI) trusted by both the IdP and RP.

nist63.title: HoK Prohibitions
nist63.statement: A holder-of-key assertion SHALL NOT include an unencrypted private key or symmetric key to be used as an authenticator.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Indicator
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL include an indicator in the assertion when the assertion is to be used with a bound authenticator at FAL3.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Uniqueness
nist63.statement: A bound authenticator SHALL be unique per subscriber at the RP such that two subscribers cannot present the same authenticator for their separate RP subscriber accounts.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Verification Timing
nist63.statement: Bound authenticators SHALL be accepted for authentication in the context of processing an FAL3 assertion for a federated transaction.

nist63.title: Pre-existing Bound Authenticator Reference in RP Subscriber Account
nist63.statement: Before an RP can successfully accept an FAL3 assertion, the RP subscriber account SHALL include a reference to a bound authenticator that is to be verified during the FAL3 transaction.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Change Notification
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL send a notification to the subscriber via an out-of-band mechanism (e.g., an email to an address previously associated with the subscriber)...if any of the following events occur: (a) A new bound authenticator is added to the RP subscriber account. (b) An existing bound authenticator is removed from the RP subscriber account.

nist63.title: Binding Ceremony Session Establishment
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL first establish an authenticated session using federation with an assertion that meets all the other requirements of FAL3, including an indication that the assertion is intended for use at FAL3 with a bound authenticator (e.g., the assertion contains an authentication class reference or a Vectors of Trust [RFC8485] value indicating this).

nist63.title: Binding Ceremony Authenticator Prompt
nist63.statement: The subscriber SHALL immediately be prompted to present and authenticate with the proposed authenticator.

nist63.title: Binding Ceremony Authenticator Identifier Storage
nist63.statement: Upon successful presentation of the authenticator, the RP SHALL store a unique identifier for the authenticator (such as its public key) and associate this with the RP subscriber account that is associated with the federated identifier.

nist63.title: Binding Ceremony Session Timeout
nist63.statement: The binding ceremony session SHALL have a timeout of five minutes or less.

nist63.title: Binding Ceremony Session Restriction
nist63.statement: The binding ceremony session... SHALL NOT be used as an authenticated session for any other purpose, as described in Sec. 3.9.

nist63.title: Post-Binding Ceremony Transaction Initiation
nist63.statement: Upon successful completion of the binding ceremony, the RP SHALL immediately request a new assertion from the IdP at FAL3.

nist63.title: Adding an Additional Bound Authenticator (1)
nist63.statement: During the initial authentication step of the binding ceremony, the RP SHALL request authentication with an existing bound authenticator to reach FAL3.

nist63.title: Adding an Additional Bound Authenticator (2)
nist63.statement: Once this authentication is complete and the binding ceremony session is established, the RP SHALL request authentication with the new authenticator and associate it with the RP subscriber account as a bound authenticator.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Removal - Session Termination
nist63.statement: When a bound authenticator is removed, the RP SHALL terminate all current FAL3 sessions for the subscriber and SHALL require reauthentication of the subscriber from the IdP at FAL3.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Removal - No Prompt for Removed Authenticator
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL NOT prompt the subscriber to authenticate with the authenticator being removed, since the subscriber will often not have access to the authenticator in question during the unbinding process, particularly if the authenticator is lost or compromised.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Verification
nist63.statement: The subscriber SHALL prove possession of the bound authenticator to the RP, in addition to presenting the assertion itself.

nist63.title: Bound Authenticator Failure Handling
nist63.statement: Failure to authenticate with the bound authenticator SHALL result in an error at the RP and SHALL NOT create an authenticated session at the RP.

nist63.title: Attribute Bundle Signing
nist63.statement: If the CSP issues attribute bundles to the RP: The CSP SHALL sign attribute bundles issued to the IdP.

nist63.title: Trust Agreement Availability to Subscribers
nist63.statement: The terms of the trust agreement SHALL be made available to subscribers upon request to the IdP or RP.

nist63.title: Subscriber-Driven Trust Agreement Disclosure Terms
nist63.statement: In a subscriber-driven trust agreement, the trust agreement takes the form of a set of terms of use as opposed to a formal contract between parties. Consequently, the following terms SHALL be disclosed to the subscriber upon request: (a) Any attribute sources from which the IdP receives applicable subscriber attributes, including the CSP. (b) Any identity APIs that are made available by the IdP, either directly or through an external provider, and which subscriber attributes are available at these APIs. (c) The set of subscriber attributes, derived attributes, and attribute bundles that the IdP can make available to the RP. (d) The attribute storage policy of the IdP for the subscriber account, including any available means for the subscriber to request deletion; the use of any shared signaling between the IdP and RP. (e) The population of subscriber accounts for which the IdP can create assertions; any additional uses of subscriber information, beyond providing the identity service; the xALs available from the IdP. (f) The xALs required by the RP.

nist63.title: Subscriber-Driven Redress Assessment Disclosure
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL assess its redress mechanisms for efficacy in resolving complaints or problems and disclose the results of this assessment to the subscriber.

nist63.title: Runtime Decision Disclosure Terms
nist63.statement: The following terms of the trust agreement SHALL be disclosed to the subscriber during the runtime decision: (a) The set of subscriber attributes, derived attributes, and attribute bundles that the RP will request (i.e., a subset of the attributes made available by the IdP). (b) The purpose for each attribute requested by the RP. (c) The attribute storage policy of the RP for the RP subscriber account, including any available means for the subscriber to request deletion.

nist63.title: Dynamic Registration Channel Protection
nist63.statement: All transmission of configuration information SHALL be made over a secure protected channel to endpoints that are associated with the IdP's identifier by the trust agreement.

nist63.title: Subscriber Authentication Before IdP Actions
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL require the subscriber to have an authenticated session before any of the following events: (a) Approval of attribute release. (b) Creation and issuance of an assertion. (c) Establishment of a subscriber-driven trust agreement.

nist63.title: Allowlist: Subscriber Availability
nist63.statement: IdPs SHALL make allowlists available to subscribers, as described in Sec. 7.2.

nist63.title: Allowlist: Additional Attribute Requests
nist63.statement: If additional attributes are requested by the RP, the request SHALL be: (a) Subject to a runtime decision of the authorized party to approve the additional attributes requested. (b) Redacted to only the attributes in the allowlist entry, or (c) Denied outright by the IdP.

nist63.title: Blocklist Assertion Prohibition
nist63.statement: If an RP is on an IdP's blocklist, the IdP SHALL NOT produce an assertion that targets the RP in question under any circumstances.

nist63.title: Blocklist: RP Identification
nist63.statement: IdP blocklists SHALL identify RPs through the means of domain names, cryptographic keys, or other identifiers that are applicable to the federation protocol in use. Any entities that share an identifier SHALL be considered equivalent for the purposes of the blocklist.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Runtime Authorization
nist63.statement: Every RP that is in a trust agreement with an IdP but not on an allowlist with that IdP SHALL be governed by a default policy in which runtime authorization decisions will be made by an authorized party that is identified by the trust agreement.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Attribute Release Consent
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL provide the authorized party with explicit notice and prompt them for positive confirmation before any attributes about the subscriber are transmitted to the RP.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Attribute Disclosure Before Release
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL disclose which attributes will be released to the RP if the transaction is approved.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Selective attribute disclosure
nist63.statement: If the federation protocol in use allows for optional or selective attribute disclosure at runtime, the authorized party SHALL be given the option to decide whether to transmit specific attributes to the RP without terminating the federation transaction entirely.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Attribute Value Viewing Mechanism
nist63.statement: If the authorized party is the subscriber, the IdP SHALL provide mechanisms for the subscriber to view the attribute values and derived attribute values to be sent to the RP.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Sensitive Information Masking
nist63.statement: To mitigate the risk of unauthorized exposure of sensitive information (e.g., shoulder surfing), the IdP SHALL, by default, mask sensitive information displayed to the subscriber.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Remembered Decision Disclosure
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL disclose to the authorized party that the storage mechanism is in use.

nist63.title: RP Not on Allowlist: Remembered Decision Revocation
nist63.statement: [The IdP] SHALL allow the authorized party to revoke such remembered access at a future time.

nist63.title: RP Blocklist: IdP Identification
nist63.statement: RP blocklists SHALL identify IdPs through domain names, cryptographic keys, or other identifiers that are applicable to the federation protocol in use. Any entities that share an identifier SHALL be considered equivalent for the purposes of the blocklist.

nist63.title: RP Runtime Decision: IdP Acceptance
nist63.statement: Every IdP that is in a trust agreement with an RP but not on an allowlist with that RP SHALL be governed by a default policy in which runtime authorization decisions will be made by the authorized party indicated in the trust agreement.

nist63.title: RP Runtime Decision: Remembered Decision Disclosure
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL disclose to the authorized party that the storage mechanism is in use.

nist63.title: RP Runtime Decision: Remembered Decision Revocation
nist63.statement: [The RP] SHALL allow the authorized party to revoke such remembered access at a future time.

nist63.title: Ephemeral Provisioning Identifier Unlinking
nist63.statement: If a federation identifier is supplied in the assertion, the RP SHALL remove any linkage of the federated identifier from an RP subscriber account.

nist63.title: RP Processing of Termination Signal
nist63.statement: Upon receiving such a signal, the RP SHALL process the RP subscriber account as stipulated in the trust agreement and in accordance with Sec. 3.11.3.

nist63.title: IdP Notification of Terminations due to Fraud or Suspicious Activity
nist63.statement: If the reason for termination is suspicious or fraudulent activity, the IdP SHALL notify the RP of the termination and include the reason in its signal to the RP to allow the RP to review the associated RP subscriber account's activity for suspicious activity, if specified in the trust agreement with that RP.

nist63.title: Provisioning API Mutual Authentication
nist63.statement: Access to the provisioning API SHALL occur over a mutually authenticated protected channel.

nist63.title: Trust Agreement Required for Provisioning API
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL NOT make a provisioning API available to any RP outside of an established trust agreement.

nist63.title: Provisioning API Access Revocation
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL revoke an RP's access to the provisioning API once access is no longer required by the RP for its functioning purposes or when the trust agreement is terminated.

nist63.title: Provisioning API Account State Change Signaling
nist63.statement: When a provisioning API is in use, the IdP SHALL signal to the RP when the state of a subscriber account has been changed, such as when the account has been terminated or disabled.

nist63.title: Federated Identifier Unbinding Upon Terminated/Disabled Signal
nist63.statement: When receiving such a signal, the RP SHALL remove the binding of the federated identifier from the account.

nist63.title: Redress for Additionally Collected Attributes
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL provide a secure and effective means of redress for the subscriber to update and remove these additionally collected attributes from the RP subscriber account.

nist63.title: Time-Based Termination Notice and Reactivation
nist63.statement: When processing an inactive account, the RP SHALL provide sufficient notice to the subscriber about the pending termination of the account and provide the subscriber with an option to re-activate the account prior to its scheduled termination.

nist63.title: Communication of Authentication Recency
nist63.statement: The IdP SHALL communicate to the RP any information that the IdP has regarding the recency of the subscriber's latest authentication event at the IdP, and the RP MAY use this information to make authorization and access decisions.

nist63.title: Identity API Access Insufficient for Session Extension
nist63.statement: The RP's ability to successfully fetch additional attributes through an identity API SHALL NOT be used to establish or extend a session at the RP.

nist63.title: Shared Signal Personal Information Minimization
nist63.statement: Shared signals SHALL NOT include personal information except what is necessary to identify the subscriber account in question (e.g., an account identifier or attributes that can be correlated by the receiving party).

nist63.title: IdP Compromise Signal Review
nist63.statement: If the IdP receives a signal that a subscriber account is suspected of compromise, the IdP SHALL review actions taken by that account at the IdP for suspicious activity.

nist63.title: Linked IdP Identity Protection in Shared Signals
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL ensure that the shared signals do not reveal the identity of a subscriber's linked IdPs.

nist63.title: Assertion Attribute Requirements
nist63.statement: All assertions SHALL include the following attributes: (1) Issuer identifier: An identifier for the issuer of the assertion (i.e., the IdP). (2) Audience identifier: An identifier for the party intended to consume the assertion (i.e., the RP). An assertion can contain more than one audience identifier at FAL1. (3) Issuance time: A timestamp that indicates when the IdP issued the assertion. (4) Validity time window: A period of time outside of which the assertion SHALL NOT be accepted as valid by the RP for the purposes of authenticating the subscriber and starting an authenticated session at the RP. This is usually communicated by means of an expiration timestamp for the assertion in addition to the issuance timestamp. (5) Assertion identifier: A value that uniquely identifies this assertion and is used to prevent attackers from replaying prior assertions. (6) Authentication time: A timestamp that indicates when the IdP last verified the presence of the subscriber at the IdP through a primary authentication event. (7) Signature: Digital signature or MAC, including verification key identifier, that covers the entire assertion.

nist63.title: Subject ID Uniqueness
nist63.statement: An RP that uses the federated identifier to identify the subscriber SHALL NOT treat subject identifiers as inherently globally unique across IdPs.

nist63.title: RP Session Time Independent of Assertion
nist63.statement: Assertion validity time windows SHALL NOT be used to limit the session at the RP. See Sec. 4.7 for more information.

nist63.title: Assertion Request Requirements
nist63.statement: When the federation transaction is initiated by the RP, the RP's request for an assertion SHALL contain: (1) An identifier for the RP. (2) A cryptographic nonce to be returned in the assertion.

nist63.title: Tamper & Fabrication Resistant Assertion References
nist63.statement: The assertion reference itself contains no information about the subscriber and SHALL be resistant to tampering and fabrication by an attacker.

nist63.title: Single-use Assertion Reference
nist63.statement: The assertion reference: 2. SHALL be single-use.

nist63.title: Assertion Reference Time Limitation
nist63.statement: The assertion reference: 3. SHALL be time-limited.

nist63.title: Subscriber Back-Channel Protection
nist63.statement: Conveyance of the assertion reference from the IdP to the subscriber and from the subscriber to the RP SHALL be made over an authenticated protected channel.

nist63.title: RP-IdP Back-Channel Protection
nist63.statement: Conveyance of the assertion reference from the RP to the IdP and vice versa SHALL be made over an authenticated protected channel.

nist63.title: Assertion Reference Injection Prevention
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL protect itself against the injection of manufactured or captured assertion references by using cross-site scripting (XSS) and cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection, rejecting assertion references outside of the correct stage of a federation transaction, or other accepted techniques discussed in Sec. 3.11.1.

nist63.title: RP Front-Channel Injection Protection
nist63.statement: The RP SHALL protect itself against the injection of manufactured or captured assertions by using XSS and CSRF protection, rejecting assertions outside of the correct stage of a federation transaction, or other accepted techniques discussed in Sec. 3.11.1.

nist63.title: Subscriber Front-Channel Protection
nist63.statement: Conveyance of the assertion from the IdP to the subscriber and from the subscriber to the RP SHALL be made over an authenticated protected channel.

nist63.title: Front-Channel Personal Information Protection
nist63.statement: As a consequence, an IdP that uses HTTP redirects for the front-channel presentation of assertions SHALL encrypt all personal information in the assertion, as discussed in Sec. 3.13.3.

nist63.title: Attribute Bundle Uniqueness
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL create a unique attribute bundle for each requesting wallet.

nist63.title: Attribute Bundle Invalidation Capability
nist63.statement: The CSP SHALL provide a means of invalidating attribute bundles that are issued to a subscriber-controlled wallet.

nist63.title: Wallet Runtime Decision Disclosure Terms
nist63.statement: 3. The following terms SHALL be disclosed to the subscriber during the runtime decision: (a) The set of subscriber attributes, derived attributes, and attribute bundles that the RP will request (a subset of the attributes made available). (b) The purpose of each attribute requested by the RP.

nist63.title: Wallet Activation for Signing Operations
nist63.statement: The subscriber-controlled wallet SHALL require the presentation of an activation factor from the subscriber for the following actions that result in the creation of a signed artifact from the wallet's signing keys: providing proof of possession of the wallet's signing key to the CSP during the issuance process; and signing the assertion for presentation to the RP.

nist63.title: Wallet Activation Separation from Device Unlock
nist63.statement: For subscriber-controlled wallets that run on a device that the subscriber controls, the submission of the activation factor SHALL be a separate operation from the unlocking of the host device (e.g., smartphone), although the same activation factor used to unlock the host device MAY be used in the activation operation.
